title: Microsoft Purview: exclude Microsoft 365 groups and target dynamic and non-mail-enabled security groups in sensitivity label policies
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing quotations and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections would complete the abbreviated control paths and cite the encryption documentation that explicitly confirms publishing exclusions do not change access to protected content.

claims.claim: Dynamic membership adds and removes users as directory attributes change.
claims.quote: When an attribute changes for a user or device, all rules for dynamic membership groups in the organization are processed for changes. Users and devices are added or removed if they meet the conditions for a dynamic membership group.

claims.claim: Policy targeting is reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... To edit an existing label policy, select it, and then select the Edit Policy button from the flyout pane:
claims.fix: Keep the documented path. Extend controls[0].note to: 'Edit Policy opens the Create policy configuration; continue through the wizard to choose the users and groups. Learn does not name that wizard page. The cmdlet reference covers mailboxes, distribution groups and mail-enabled security groups.'

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -AddExchangeLocation "<mailbox>" adds a mailbox to the policy scope.
claims.quote: The AddExchangeLocation parameter specifies the mailboxes to add to the list of included mailboxes when you aren't using the value All for the ExchangeLocation parameter. A valid value is a mailbox.

claims.claim: The Set-LabelPolicy reference documents scope changes for mailboxes, distribution groups and mail-enabled security groups.
claims.quote: The RemoveExchangeLocation parameter specifies the mailboxes to remove from the list of included mailboxes ... Valid values are: A mailbox; A distribution group or mail-enabled security group (all mailboxes that are currently members of the group).

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 group exclusion is reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy.
claims.quote: To edit an existing label policy, select it, and then select the Edit Policy button from the flyout pane: ... This action starts the Create policy configuration
claims.fix: Keep the documented path and append to controls[1].note: 'Edit Policy opens the Create policy configuration; continue through the wizard to choose group exclusions. Learn does not name that wizard page.' The cited sensitivity-labels overview confirms group exclusions.

claims.fix: Replace controls[2].ui.path and the matching table path with 'Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Actions > Move up or Move down'. The existing sensitivity-labels source names those two options.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -NextLabelPolicy "<policy name>" changes policy order.
claims.quote: The NextLabelPolicy parameter updates the policy order so the policy that's specified by this parameter is after the current policy that you're modifying. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the policy. For example: Name

claims.claim: Move up and Move down are the policy reordering actions.
claims.quote: To reorder the label policies, select a sensitivity label policy, choose the Actions ellipsis for that entry, and then select Move down or Move up.

claims.claim: Access to content encrypted by a label is governed by the label's encryption settings.
